definition_quote.value: "practice of medicine" or "practice of osteopathy" means: (A) for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition; or to attempt to perform or represent that a person is authorized to perform any of the acts set out in this subparagraph; (B) to use or publicly display a title in connection with a person's name including "doctor of medicine," "physician," "M.D.," or "doctor of osteopathic medicine" or "D.O." or a specialist designation
definition_quote.quote: "practice of medicine" or "practice of osteopathy" means: (A) for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition

methods_authorized.quote: to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe, dispense, and administer prescription drugs including controlled substances, subject to limits on opioid prescriptions (7-day supply for initial prescriptions) and telehealth prescribing rules.
drug_authority.quote: prescribing, dispensing, or administering a prescription drug that is a controlled substance

license_status_types.quote: A licensee who does not practice in the state may hold an inactive license ... On retiring from practice ... a licensee in good standing with the board may apply for the conversion of an active or inactive license to a retired status license ... the board may issue a temporary permit ... a temporary permit for locum tenens practice ... the board may issue a permit to an applicant without examination ... for the limited purpose of residency or internship

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must meet requirements of AS 08.64.200(a)(3)-(5) and 08.64.255, complete three years of postgraduate training (or alternative board-approved requirements), and pass examinations as specified by the board. Alternative proof of competency may include current licensure in another state with active practice for at least three years, or current board certification by the American Board of Medical Specialties.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Applicants who are graduates of medical colleges not accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association shall ... have successfully completed three years of postgraduate training

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: two years if the applicant graduated from medical school on or after January 1, 1995

pain_management_education_required.quote: receive education in pain management and opioid use and addiction, unless the applicant has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the board that the applicant does not currently hold a valid federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Initial opioid prescriptions for adult outpatients may not exceed a seven-day supply. Prescriptions for minors may not exceed a seven-day supply. Exceptions exist for acute medical conditions, chronic pain, cancer pain, palliative care, logistical/travel barriers, and treatment of substance abuse or opioid dependence.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: A licensee may not issue an initial prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day supply to an adult patient for outpatient use; a prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day supply to a minor

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: require that a licensee who has a federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number register with the controlled substance prescription database under AS 17.30.200(n)

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A physician or physician assistant may prescribe non-controlled substances via telehealth without a physical examination if follow-up care is available and records are sent to the primary care provider with patient consent. Controlled substances may also be prescribed if those conditions and AS 08.64.363 are met. A physician may not prescribe abortion-inducing drugs via telehealth without complying with AS 18.16.010. Neither a physician nor PA may prescribe in response to an Internet questionnaire or email to a person with whom they have no prior physician-patient relationship.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The board may not impose disciplinary sanctions on a physician or physician assistant for rendering a diagnosis, providing treatment, or prescribing, dispensing, or administering a prescription drug that is not a controlled substance to a person without conducting a physical examination if the physician, physician assistant, or another licensed health care provider in the medical practice is available to provide follow-up care

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: a physician assistant may examine, diagnose, or treat persons under the supervision, control, and responsibility of either a physician licensed under this chapter or a physician exempted from licensing under AS 08.64.370

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may prescribe, dispense, or administer prescription drugs including controlled substances under the supervision, control, and responsibility of a licensed physician, subject to board regulations and the same telehealth prescribing rules as physicians.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: adopt regulations regarding the licensure of physician assistants and the medical services that they may perform, including the ... scope of activities authorized

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: A person licensed under this chapter shall report in writing to the board concerning the outcome of each medical malpractice claim or civil action in which damages have been or are to be paid by or on behalf of the licensee to the claimant or plaintiff

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A hospital that revokes, suspends, conditions, restricts, or refuses to grant hospital privileges to, or imposes a consultation requirement on, a person licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy in the state shall report to the board the name and address of the person and the reasons for the action within seven working days after the action is taken.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: contract with private professional organizations to establish an impaired medical professionals program to identify, confront, evaluate, and treat persons licensed under this chapter who abuse alcohol, other drugs, or other substances or are mentally ill or cognitively impaired

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: the board may order a person to whom it has issued a license or permit to submit to a medical or psychiatric examination by a physician or other practitioner of the healing arts appointed by the board

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: A member of the board, its executive secretary, or a person designated by the board to issue temporary permits may grant a temporary permit to a physician or osteopath for the purpose of substituting for another physician or osteopath licensed in this state

investigational_drug_protection.quote: A physician may not be subject to disciplinary action by the board for prescribing, dispensing, or administering an investigational drug, biological product, or device, or providing related treatment, to a patient for the purpose of sustaining the patient's life if the patient has a terminal illness

scope__license_status_types.quote: A licensee who does not practice in the state may hold an inactive license.

On retiring from practice and payment of an appropriate one-time fee, a licensee in good standing with the board may apply for the conversion of an active or inactive license to a retired status license.

suspend a license for a determinate period of time
permanently revoke a license to practice
